author: y. m. yates
title: Webster responds to President Trump's address on Operation Epic Fury progress
text:
Florida Congressman Daniel Webster released a statement on Apr. 1 in response to President Trump’s national address regarding Operation Epic Fury. Webster, a Republican from Clermont, commented on the objectives and progress of the military operation against Iran.
The issue is significant as it addresses U.S. foreign policy and military action aimed at countering threats from the Iranian regime and preventing nuclear proliferation.
“For 47 years, the Iranian regime has chanted for the death of our country, murdered American service members, brutalized their own citizens, and terrorized the world,” Webster said in his statement. He continued: “When President Trump announced Operation Epic Fury 32 days ago, he set clear objectives: End the threat of the Iranian terrorist regime and their proxies, destroy their military capabilities, ensure that Iran never obtains a nuclear weapon.”
Webster also referenced recent developments in the operation. “Tonight, President Trump announced that in just one month, our armed forces have made tremendous progress in accomplishing these objectives. The United States military has once again proven to be the most lethal fighting force in the world, and I continue to pray for our service members.”
Webster is currently serving as U.S. Representative for Florida’s 11th district after replacing Alan Grayson in 2011 according to official records . He has held this position since 2011; prior to his congressional tenure he served in both chambers of Florida’s legislature between 1980 and 2008 according to public information.
Born in Charleston, West Virginia in 1949 and now residing in Clermont at age 74, Webster graduated from Georgia Institute of Technology with a Bachelor of Science degree in 1971.
As developments around Operation Epic Fury continue to unfold following President Trump’s announcement and congressional responses like Webster’s statement emerge publicly, observers are likely to monitor both legislative reactions and further updates from U.S. officials.
